sections.skill: Compare AI roles with a film crew

questions.prompt: Film editors who cut what does not work are like whom?
questions.intro: A movie needs more than camera operators. WRITERS decide the story, like product managers deciding what a tool does. EDITORS review footage and cut what does not work, like evaluators. RESEARCH STAFF check historical details, like subject experts. LAWYERS clear rights, like governance roles. AI work is similar: the people writing code are one part of a larger team.

sections.skill: Weigh technical literacy and job conditions

questions.prompt: Why do non-coding AI roles still need technical literacy?

choices.text: Because every non-coding role secretly requires writing large amounts of code each day
To understand how AI works and fails

questions.correct_answer: To understand how AI works and fails
questions.intro: Non-coding roles still need some technical literacy: understanding what models can and cannot do, how they fail, and how to describe problems precisely. A nurse who can explain why an AI summary of a patient chart is unsafe is very valuable. Some data-labeling jobs are low-paid and repetitive, so look at conditions as well as titles. Combining your existing field with AI understanding is often a stronger route than switching fields entirely.
